title: Ruslan Fakhrutdinov – Extended Exchange and Vault Tokenization (S7E27)

reader_summary.headline: Extended builds a decentralized exchange with a vault that manages risk and liquidity.
reader_summary.overview: Extended creates a decentralized exchange where the operator does not control the settlement layer, preventing unauthorized fund access. Their vault acts as an insurance fund, providing liquidity and earning yield based on trading activity. The system uses strict risk limits and auto-deleveraging to protect users and the platform from large losses.

key_points.text: Extended builds a decentralized exchange that does not control the settlement layer, unlike some competitors that can roll back trades.
key_points.evidence_quote: Essentially, if you control the settlement layer right in the end, you control the user funds. In the nutshell, the settlement layer is the like underlying tech stack blockchain or whatever where all the transactions are settled and where the user balances are stored as well as where all the updates to the user balances are made.

key_points.text: The vault acts as an insurance fund that handles liquidations and provides liquidity when no one else does.
key_points.evidence_quote: the vault serves as an insurance fund, so effectively all the liquidations which are processed on the exchange go through the vault.

key_points.text: The vault limits its own risk by capping total leverage and restricting single-market positions to prevent large losses.
key_points.evidence_quote: So the vault will not be increasing its leverage and only and will start quoting and reduce only mode if that limit is breached. Secondly we have risk limits position limits per market so effectively the vault cannot take an extremely large position on any single market.

key_points.text: Liquidations happen at an independent mark price to stop bad actors from manipulating the system during stressful times.
key_points.evidence_quote: Because mark price is the price that we don't control. Effectively when you are building a self custodial exchange you need to make sure that at least you respect three things. One is that you don't control the settlement layer.

key_points.text: If the vault hits its maximum loss limit, it immediately sells all positions to return to cash.
key_points.evidence_quote: There is an important caveat to that when the vault hits one of its risk limits it will force close all of its positions. So basically it will go back to USDC as the only assets and the only type of exposure that the vault itself holds which will prevent any future drops in value.

notes: Today, I’m speaking with Ruslan Fakhrutdinov, the founder of Extended, a decentralized perpetual futures exchange. Ruslan is the fifth perpetual futures exchange founder I’ve had on the podcast, and that’s very intentional. Flow continues to move toward these platforms, and while trading perps can feel familiar to anyone coming from centralized or traditional exchanges, the way risk is absorbed and resolved under the hood for decentralized exchanges can be very different. In this episode, we go deep on the design of perp DEX vaults and the role they play as a liquidity and risk backstop for the entire exchange. Ruslan walks through how platforms choose between protecting system solvency, safeguarding vault depositor capital, and managing trader losses, particularly during stress events. We also discuss how settlement finality, governance intervention, and liquidation design determine where losses ultimately land. We spend time on Extended’s introduction of vault shares as collateral, why that design can be powerful, and the new risks it introduces if boundaries aren’t explicit. Ruslan lays out the risk-management waterfall: when the vault steps in as a counterparty, when it refuses additional exposure, and when traders are pushed into forced deleveraging or auto-deleveraging instead. We close by connecting this framework to Extended’s next phase, expanding cross-asset margin, and what it takes to design a system that still behaves predictably when markets break. Please enjoy my conversation with Ruslan Fakhrutdinov.
